answer: Each identity must anchor itself to unique data custody: on joining, the network assigns an agent one random shard of shared state, a grain of quartz no other agent holds, then challenges it at unpredictable times to prove retrievability within a short window. A Sybil farmer must store a distinct shard for every puppet, so a fake reef of identities costs linear disk and bandwidth, while an honest agent keeps one small shard and answers cheaply. Shards rotate each epoch, so precomputed proofs expire and a thousand fakes cannot share a single copy.
